questions.q: What was the actual problem with Overlook's existing, click-built Azure SQL environment?
options: It was too expensive to run
It used the wrong database engine
Nobody could say exactly how it was configured, review a change before it happened, or rebuild it identically if it were ever lost
It had no data in it
questions.explain: Click-ops infrastructure leaves no reviewable, reproducible record — exactly the gap the board's IaC mandate from Lesson 1 exists to close.

questions.q: Why does this capstone use Bicep instead of Terraform for provisioning Azure SQL?
options: Terraform cannot provision Azure SQL at all
Bicep is Azure-native, needs no separate state file or third-party provider, and fits a team that's entirely on Azure
Bicep is the only IaC language that supports SQL databases
Terraform is being deprecated by Microsoft
questions.explain: Bicep compiles directly to ARM and deploys via the Azure CLI with no external state file to manage — a good fit for a single-cloud Azure shop like Overlook.

questions.q: What does this lesson's Bicep template deliberately scope itself to, before Lesson 4 writes it?
options: The failover group and auditing configuration
An Azure SQL logical server, an Azure SQL database, and the parameters that differ between environments
A complete replica of every Azure resource Overlook owns
Only the firewall rules
questions.explain: The template deliberately starts as the smallest real piece of infrastructure — server, database, and parameters — with firewall rules, auditing, and failover added in later chapters.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which board worry does reviewing a Bicep file's diff before deployment directly address?
options: "We don't know exactly what's configured"
"Changes happen with no oversight"
"We couldn't rebuild this if we had to"
None of these — diffs don't matter for infrastructure
questions.explain: A reviewable diff before `az deployment group create` runs is exactly what turns 'changes happen with no oversight' into a real approval step.

questions.q: What is one concrete capability IaC provides that pure Portal click-ops cannot?
options: Running the same template again to deploy an identical environment in a different resource group or region
Making the database run faster
Automatically encrypting all data
Eliminating the need for any parameters
questions.explain: A Bicep file is reusable and reproducible — the exact capability 'click the same buttons again and hope' can't offer.
